signal: Coagulant dose drifted off jar-test target, since corrected
aiInterpretation: Pump output drifted ~15% low over two hours; settled water turbidity was trending up before correction.

detail.signal: Coagulant dose on T02 drifted from 18.1 to 15.4 mg/L between 09:40 and 11:30, without a corresponding jar-test change.
detail.observed: Coagulant pump output declined gradually; no operator setpoint change logged in the same window.
detail.derived: Settled water turbidity downstream began rising within 40 minutes of the dose drop — consistent with underdosing, not a raw water change.
detail.inferred: Pump wear or a partially fouled injection point is the leading theory — confirmed by inspection and corrected.
detail.recommendation: Recalibrate the coagulant feed pump and confirm dose against a fresh jar test before returning to automatic control.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Coagulant feed pump was recalibrated at 11:38 after inspection found early signs of diaphragm wear.
detail.risk: Low — caught before filtered water turbidity was affected
detail.expectedOutcome: Coagulant dose restored to jar-test target

signal: Sludge blanket rose toward the weir, desludging caught it up
aiInterpretation: Blanket climbed for over an hour as desludging fell behind normal frequency; corrected before any carryover risk.

detail.signal: Sludge blanket level on T04 rose from 33% to 58% of basin depth between 10:20 and 12:10, while the desludge cycle ran less frequently than its normal interval.
detail.observed: Blanket level trending up steadily; desludge cycle frequency below the typical rate for current raw water loading.
detail.derived: The rise rate tracks almost linearly with the missed desludge cycles — a scheduling gap, not a sudden solids loading event.
detail.inferred: Desludge cycle timer was not adjusted after a raw water turbidity increase earlier in the shift — corrected manually.
detail.recommendation: Run an extra desludge cycle and re-check the auto-cycle timer logic against current raw water turbidity.
detail.whatChangedSummary: An extra manual desludge cycle at 12:10 reversed the rise within 30 minutes.
detail.confidence: Confirmed — blanket responded immediately to the extra cycle
detail.risk: Low — resolved well before weir overflow risk
detail.expectedOutcome: Blanket level returned to normal operating range

signal: Filter headloss climbing, run time shortening
aiInterpretation: Headloss has risen steadily since shift start with no matching turbidity spike — media fouling, not an upstream upset.

detail.signal: Headloss on T01's filter has climbed from 2.6 to 4.4 ft since 08:30, with run time between backwashes shortening from a typical 48 hours toward roughly 30.
detail.observed: Headloss rising at a steady rate; filter effluent turbidity remains within spec throughout.
detail.derived: Because effluent quality hasn't degraded, this reads as physical media fouling accumulating, not a process upset that would show up in turbidity first.
detail.inferred: Progressive media fouling — most likely mudball formation or media loss reducing effective bed depth, pending the next scheduled bed inspection.
detail.recommendation: Schedule a filter bed inspection before the next backwash; consider an early backwash if headloss approaches the 6 ft alarm point.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Raw water turbidity increase considered and rejected — intake readings have been stable all shift.

detail.whatChangedSummary: No triggering event identified yet — the rise has been gradual since the start of the shift.
detail.risk: Medium — approaching a shortened backwash cycle if the trend continues
detail.expectedOutcome: Bed inspection scheduled for next available window

signal: Settled water turbidity sensor drift, confirmed against grab sample
aiInterpretation: Sensor read erratically for nearly an hour while a manual grab sample stayed flat — a measurement fault, not a real turbidity event.

detail.signal: The settled-water turbidimeter on T05 swung between 1.8 and 4.6 NTU from 09:35, while a manual grab sample taken at 10:20 read a steady 2.0 NTU.
detail.observed: Turbidity signal varies rapidly in both directions; manual grab sample and downstream filter performance both remain steady.
detail.derived: Filter effluent never responded to the swings — a real 4.6 NTU settled-water event would show up there within the hydraulic residence time.
detail.inferred: Instrument fouling or a loose sample line connection, not a real process swing — confirmed by cleaning and recalibrating the sensor.
detail.recommendation: Validate the instrument against a grab sample on this schedule going forward; flag for cleaning during next PM cycle.

relatedOccurrences.summary: True settled-water turbidity event considered and rejected — filter effluent never moved.

detail.whatChangedSummary: A grab sample at 10:20 confirmed the mismatch, and the sensor was cleaned shortly after.

whatChanged.description: Grab sample taken, compared to sensor.

detail.risk: Low — measurement-only, no real process risk
detail.expectedOutcome: Sensor agreement with grab sample restored

signal: Storm event raw water turbidity shock, absorbed without a filtered-water impact
aiInterpretation: Raw water turbidity spiked sharply during a storm cell; coagulant dose was increased in response and no downstream exceedance occurred.

detail.signal: Raw water turbidity on the T03 intake spiked from a baseline of 9 NTU to 68 NTU between 10:30 and 12:40, coinciding with a recorded storm cell over the watershed.
detail.observed: Raw turbidity rose sharply; coagulant dose was manually increased partway through the event.
detail.derived: The turbidity rise and dose increase are tightly correlated in time, and settled/filtered water never exceeded spec — the response kept pace with the shock.
detail.inferred: A storm-driven raw water quality shock, successfully absorbed by an early coagulant dose increase — consistent with known seasonal storm response patterns.
detail.recommendation: Log this event for the seasonal storm-response playbook; no further action needed this shift.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Coagulant dose was manually increased at 11:48 in response to the rising raw water turbidity.
detail.confidence: Confirmed — dose response tracked the raw water signal closely
detail.risk: High while active — real risk of a filtered-water exceedance if the response had lagged
detail.expectedOutcome: Raw water and coagulant dose both returned to baseline

signal: Filter backwashing more often than its normal cycle
aiInterpretation: Backwash frequency has roughly doubled since late morning — each cycle looks routine alone, the pattern is what matters.

detail.signal: T06 has backwashed 5 times since 11:00, roughly twice its typical rate for this time of day, though headloss and effluent turbidity both recover fully after each cycle.
detail.observed: Backwash frequency elevated; each individual cycle completes normally with full recovery.
detail.derived: No single backwash looks abnormal — the significance is in the accumulated frequency, not any one event.
detail.inferred: Possible early media degradation or a slightly undersized run-time setpoint for current raw water conditions — not yet confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Monitor through end of shift; if frequency continues, schedule a media condition check on this filter specifically.

detail.whatChangedSummary: No single triggering change — frequency has been elevated since about 11:00 without one clear cause yet.
detail.risk: Medium — increased backwash water usage and reduced net production if it continues
detail.expectedOutcome: Still active as of the latest cycle

signal: Contact basin maintenance underway, CT margin narrowing
aiInterpretation: Planned baffle maintenance has reduced usable contact time; CT is still above the regulatory minimum but with a smaller margin than usual.

detail.signal: Planned contact basin baffle maintenance on T02 since 13:00 has reduced effective contact time from 35 to 29 minutes, bringing the actual CT value to 128 against a required minimum of 120.
detail.observed: Contact time reduced during planned maintenance; chlorine residual unchanged.
detail.derived: CT is calculated directly from residual and contact time — the margin narrowed because contact time dropped, not because dosing changed.
detail.inferred: Expected consequence of planned maintenance, not a fault — but the margin is real and worth tracking until the basin returns to full configuration.
detail.recommendation: Monitor CT each 15-minute cycle until baffle maintenance completes; increase residual slightly if the margin narrows further.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Planned baffle maintenance is the direct, known cause of the narrowing margin.
detail.confidence: Confirmed — CT drop matches the maintenance window exactly
detail.risk: Low today, but margin is genuinely thinner than normal
detail.expectedOutcome: CT expected to recover once baffle maintenance completes
